text: Aristocracy: Ger. Aristocratie ; Fr. aristocratie ; Ital. aristocrazia . (1) A form of government in which the sovereign power is vested in a select number of individuals. (2) Those individuals and the class to which they belong. By derivation 'government of the best,' either singular or plural. Plato and Aristotle distinguish it from oligarchy (government of the few, in a bad sense), and it has still a better flavour. The commonest sense now is a class superior in birth and breeding to the other classes in a state, whether retaining special political privileges or not. For the difficulty of an exact definition see C. Lewis, Polit . Terms , x. 73. Literature : MONTESQUIEU, Esprit de Lois, II. iii, cf. III. iii, iv; ARISTOTLE, Pol., iv. 6; HALLECK, Int. Law, i. chap. vi. § I. ( J.B .)
